findings.topic: Shuttle Grant Stolen by Browser Extensions
findings.section: Phase 3 — Default-Deny Security Model and Zero-Friction Token
findings.message: Writing an HTML file to disk and opening it in the default browser is a fragile bootstrap path. Many browser extensions (AV scanners, link previewers, ad blockers) proactively read local file contents or aggressively pre-fetch URLs found in them. Because the claim grant is single-use, if an extension pre-fetches the `127.0.0.1:<port>/claim` URL with the payload before the actual page script executes, the grant is consumed in the background. The user's actual browser tab will then fail to authenticate, breaking the 'working instance' promise and requiring manual intervention or restarts.

findings.topic: Self-Signed TLS Exposes Pairing Code to MitM
findings.section: Phase 3 — Default-Deny Security Model and Zero-Friction Token
findings.message: The exposure matrix allows `--i-understand-exposure` with a self-signed TLS cert and prints the fingerprint for 'out-of-band pinning'. However, modern web browsers have no UI to manually pin a certificate fingerprint. A collaborator connecting remotely will simply click 'Proceed to unsafe' to bypass the browser warning, meaning they will unknowingly accept a Man-in-the-Middle's certificate. They will then type the 10-minute pairing code into the MitM's page, allowing the attacker to intercept the code and instantly steal the session cookie. This violates the 'safe to expose' mandate.

findings.topic: Update Transaction Bricks on Diverged Local Branch
findings.section: Phase 4 — Deny-by-Default Bundle Builder, Scrubbed Release Topology, and the Update Transaction
findings.message: The auto-update transaction assumes `git merge --ff-only origin/release` will always succeed on a tree that has been auto-stashed. This is false. If the collaborator locally commits a change instead of leaving it in the working tree, their local `release` branch will diverge from `origin/release`. The `ff-only` merge will fail, the transaction will rollback, and the collaborator will be permanently stuck on vN. They will be forced to manually run `git reset --hard` or `git rebase` to un-brick the update path, explicitly violating the 'zero operator-typed git commands after first contact' North Star criterion.

findings.section: Phase 7 — Release Integrity, the First-Contact Trust Anchor, and the External Red-Team Gate
findings.message: The threat model explicitly assumes the repo (including its docs) is attacker-controlled at clone time. If the out-of-band channel only delivers the three values (key fingerprint, tag name, commit hash) but relies on the repo's own `README.md` to provide the `git verify-commit` instructions, the attacker will simply rewrite `README.md` to omit the ceremony and instruct the user to run `anchor onboard` directly. The out-of-band communication MUST include the exact shell commands for the ceremony, not just the values, otherwise the trust anchor is bypassed trivially.
